clue.text: Second message implying flight will shortly depart on winter sports holiday?

parts.words: message implying flight will shortly depart
parts.note: the airport announcement 'now boarding' tells passengers their flight is about to leave

explanation.surface: An airport announcement at the start of a skiing trip tells travellers their plane is about to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding a board down the slopes is, as the question mark admits, likely to be away on a winter sports trip.

clue.text: Firm opening in small close politician's to exclude

parts.note: a close is an end

indicators.note: in says the firm and the opening sit inside the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
CO is short for company, a firm
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A politician scheming to shut a rival out of a small business launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' reads as a verb beside 'small', but it is a noun meaning an end. The firm-plus-opening pair is what 'in' places within the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them, shutting them out socially.

clue.text: Likely end for Russian Fed cup players, targets for male seed?

definitions.text: Likely end for Russian Fed cup players
definitions.meaning: Russian women tennis players often have surnames ending this way, as in Sharapova or Kuznetsova; the Fed Cup is the women's team competition
egg cells are what sperm seeks to fertilise

explanation.surface: Tennis talk about Russian women players being seeded in a cup draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seed' plays on tennis seeding while meaning sperm.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminine Russian surnames take this ending, and the word is also the plural of ovum, the egg cell a sperm fertilises.

clue.text: Doing porridge for 21's not simple, ultimately

parts.note: to be behind someone is to be for them, supporting them

indicators.note: not tells us to take a letter away from the word before it

parts.note: the answer to 21 means naked, so bare, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of simple

explanation.surface: Someone eating oats for breakfast is told it is more complicated than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence. 'not' removes E, the last letter of 'simple', from BARES to leave BARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving a prison sentence means being locked up in a cell, which is the idiom for jailed.

clue.text: Mission prepared after short period of time

parts.note: dishes prepared after a style are prepared à la it, the French phrase used on menus
a mo is a moment, short for a short time

explanation.surface: A mission got ready just a moment ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in Texas was a Spanish mission, famous for the 1836 siege.

clue.text: User of last of soap indeed out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are jumbled up
last of picks the final letter of soap

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone using up the last of the soap was really out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges OF, P (from 'last of soap') and INDEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug addict is a user of narcotics, which the old slang phrase describes.

clue.text: Loves a boy from Scandinavia

definitions.meaning: love is zero in tennis, so loves are zeros

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian lad is very fond of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means nothing in tennis scoring, and the plural also happens to be a Norwegian or Swedish male first name.

clue.text: Articles typically put in this container — beer going in special one

indicators.note: going in says the container and beer go inside the special one

parts.note: José Mourinho, the football manager, called himself the Special One
an urn is a container
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A list of what fits in a box, with beer added to a special one.
explanation.walkthrough: José Mourinho, a football manager well known in Britain, named himself 'the Special One'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hackneyed style of newspapers is what news articles are typically written in.

clue.text: Turning deathly pale, girl, on removal of a large organ?

indicators.note: turning says the letters of these words are twisted round into a new order
on removal of says a letter must be taken out before the rest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl goes white as an organ is removed in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange DEATHLY PALE GIRL less one L, for 'a large'. 'Organ' is a newspaper, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is called an organ, a mouthpiece for opinions, and this is a British daily broadsheet.

clue.text: Girl's turned high-maintenance, discarding much clothing

indicators.note: turned says the stretch is read backwards
stripping away most of the outer letters leaves a small middle stretch of the word

explanation.surface: A demanding girl who has taken off most of her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarding much clothing' keeps only HMAIN from the middle of 'high-maintenance'; 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Irish female first name, pronounced Neeve.

clue.text: Shock when running into toilets and meeting a horse!

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: running into says the two words collide and overlap, sharing one letter where they meet

parts.note: loos are toilets

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to bump into a horse in the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running into' makes APPAL and LOOS overlap on the shared L, so it appears once.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North American breed of horse known for its spotted coat.

clue.text: Essential to what a king of France is doing

indicators.note: Essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about what a French king is up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is to mimic them, and taking off is impersonating.

clue.text: Part of kitchen lit (all but ceiling) amid rising gloom

indicators.note: amid says one piece sits in the middle of the other
rising, in a down clue, says the word reads upwards

parts.note: murk is gloom

indicators.note: all but ceiling says the top letter of the down word is dropped

parts.note: lit, as a bird lights on a branch, means settled

explanation.surface: A dim kitchen where the light barely reaches the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen' is slang for an orchestra's percussion section. 'rising' turns MURK to KRUM; 'all but ceiling' drops the S from SETTLED, giving ETTLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral players call the percussion section the kitchen, and timpani are part of it.

clue.text: Head abandoning lesson for exam

indicators.note: head abandoning says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: A headteacher walks out of a lesson to set a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, such as a language viva, is a kind of examination.

clue.text: Mark circle outside gym for running

indicators.note: outside says the mark and circle wrap round the gym

parts.note: a scar is a mark
a ring is a circle
PE, physical education, is gym class

explanation.surface: A circle marked out on the ground beside a gym for runners.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARRING is split around PE. To scarper is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarpering is British slang for fleeing in a hurry, running away.

clue.text: Country dweller's place not to be getting on public transport in German city

indicators.note: not to be says the getting-on piece is taken away

parts.note: a cottage is a rural home
getting on means ageing
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A villager stays at home rather than catching a bus into a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to be' removes AGE from COTTAGE, leaving COTT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in Brandenburg, eastern Germany, near the Polish border.

clue.text: Can carrier from S African province depart in a day?

indicators.note: in says the province and departing go inside the day

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
the Cape was a province of South Africa
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: A man carrying a tin travels from South Africa in a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry the can is a British idiom for taking the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries the can takes the blame for others, which is exactly what a fall guy does.

clue.text: Spell of weakness after ceding power

indicators.note: after ceding says the power letter is given up

parts.note: a penchant is a weakness for something, a fondness

explanation.surface: A spell of weakness after someone gives up power.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell, in its old sense, is to bewitch with a charm, so to put under a spell.

clue.text: Have a reason not to do something?

definitions.meaning: to have someone is to trick or swindle them

definitions.text: a reason not to do something?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they have grounds to avoid a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had is to be fooled, a swindle; and in pros and cons, the second is the argument against.

clue.text: Run a live broadcast with first-rate acoustic aids

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread about

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
A, as in A1, means first-rate

explanation.surface: A radio station runs a live show with top-quality sound equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges R, A and LIVE into VELARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Awnings over Roman theatres, which some say helped carry sound, are the plural of velarium.

clue.text: Naturalist's not done much to conceal article in flat

indicators.note: in says the trimmed piece sits inside the flat one

parts.note: flat means dull

indicators.note: to conceal says the article is hidden away, taken out

parts.note: meat not cooked much is rare
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A naturalist has barely tidied up and hides something in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' here means the article vanishes from the undercooked word rather than being wrapped up; 'in' then places what is left within the flat one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Durrell was a British naturalist and zoo founder; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Letter from Greek and from Parisian, revealing all

parts.note: nu is the Greek letter N
de is French for from

explanation.surface: A letter in Greek and French that tells everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing nothing reveals their whole body, naked.

clue.text: Flower given by one say in another's seasonal gift

indicators.note: in says the flower and first example go inside the other

parts.note: another example is a second EG
an aster is a flower
say, as in for example, is EG

explanation.surface: Flowers given one by one as presents for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one say' and 'another' both stand for the same abbreviation for 'for example', so it appears twice, one copy wrapped around the flower and the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg is given as a present at the spring Christian festival.

clue.text: Sound relieved perhaps to hand over phone in ME location

indicators.note: over the phone means heard rather than seen, so the words are pronounced

parts.note: a sigh is the sound someone relieved might make; nigh means near, close to hand

explanation.surface: A relieved caller passes over a phone somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is short for Middle East. 'Sound' looks like the homophone signal but belongs to the sigh; 'over phone' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula and mountain in Egypt lie in the Middle East.

clue.text: One used to cut radio's commercials

indicators.note: on the radio a word is only heard, so it sounds like another

parts.note: ads are commercials

explanation.surface: A radio station trims its commercial breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking tool with an arched blade, for shaping timber.

clue.text: Set of ties going with neck that's lower for convenience

parts.note: a round of a cup competition is a set of ties, matches
to neck a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: Neckties and a low-cut collar picked for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower a number to a tidier figure is to round it toward the smaller value.

clue.text: One problem for dentist, briefly in GP's place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, losing its end

parts.note: a molar is a tooth a dentist may treat

explanation.surface: A dentist has a problem quickly visiting a doctor's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: GP looks like a family doctor but is a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in Italy hosts a motor racing circuit that staged Grand Prix races.

clue.text: Japanese band did pop off one

parts.note: ob., from Latin obiit, means died, as on gravestones; to pop off is to die
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Japanese pop group lost one member.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash worn round a kimono is a wide fabric belt.

clue.text: Republican hopeful of righting wrong with new chapter

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A political hopeful promising to right wrongs with a new chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a former US House Speaker who ran for the Republican presidential nomination in 2012.
